items.title: Jason Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. There’s also the Barbarin family.

ctx.x: Yeah. There’s also the Barbarin family.

Paul Barbarin. I’m a drummer. I understand that. There’s so many. But I just singled out a few. Do you see that Katrina has – what impact do you think Katrina has on this culture that is so associated and indelible to New Orleans’ musical culture?

Honestly, I don’t think it did anything in terms of music lineage. There’s some logistics that maybe got affected, in terms of business things that got affected. There was somebody that was talking about how there were different musicians that weren’t on the scene, that came in. They may have taken advantage of some things, or – there’s that. There’s some guys that did leave. There’s logistics. But the reason why I say that the music, to me, wasn’t affected, was because it was December, after the storm, and I was…
